key_insight: A physics-informed neural network can reconstruct high-resolution flow fields from sparse or noisy measurements by enforcing incompressible Navier-Stokes physics.
engineering_relevance: This improves estimation of clinically important hemodynamic indicators such as pressure and wall shear stress from under-resolved experimental flow data.
method: Combine experimental velocity measurements with Navier-Stokes constraints in a PINN.
Use the model to infer unmeasured fields and sharpen spatial resolution near difficult regions like vessel walls.
Test on both the FDA nozzle benchmark and an aneurysm blood-flow case.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports better agreement with ground truth than standard CFD or pure data-driven methods on both in silico and in vitro data.
watch_item: Performance depends on measurement quality and physics-model assumptions, so noisy data or mismatched boundary conditions may limit reconstruction accuracy.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for the High-Resolution Reconstruction of Flow Measurement Indicators in Fluid Dynamics
